keyFindings.description: The new push bound is bypassed when the give-up's exception publish fails. publishNoHolderExceptionOrNak (delivery.go:276-287) clears the attempt-cache entry, NAKs for 30 s and returns false; the caller at :870-871 returns before any give-up record, counter or line is written. The next delivery therefore has neither a dedupe entry nor an attempt entry and reaches session.HandleAgentMessage at :742-744, pushing again, before either delivery-count limit is read - unplaceableMaxDeliveries guards only the deferral branch. The cycle can run to the durable's consumerMaxDeliver of 20 with no unplaceable_push_failed counter and no give-up line ever written. So 'delivered at most twice' (delivery.go:593-604, internal/session/handler.go:33-40, docs/architecture.md) is false on a reachable path, and the path is correlated with the fault: a bus that cannot take the exception is the same bus whose trouble produced the unplaceable delivery. A permanent refusal reaches it too, since the exception embeds the original payload (delivery.go:151-175), so an accepted envelope near the payload limit yields an exception the bus refuses as too large. Both thermonuclear passes found this independently; verified in the code by the reviewer. Remedy constraint: once the push allowance is spent, retrying the notice must not restore the state that permits another push, and the terminal accounting must survive the retry.

A core publish is emitted before its deadline is checked, so an already-expired context sends the message and then reports failure. publishCoreTo (nats.go:870-886) takes deadline from the caller's context, ensureConnWithContext (nats.go:599-607) returns nil at once on a healthy connection without consulting ctx, and publishConfirmed calls publish(msg) at confirm.go:31 before computing remaining at :34, which is then <= 0 and returns 'window elapsed before the publish was flushed'. Before this pull request PublishCoreTo always built a fresh publishBound context, so the deadline could not already be spent at entry; PublishWithin introduces the path. It is reachable from publishHandler: the route's 3.5 s context starts at api.go:849 but resolveLiveRoleHolder (api.go:910) does not take it - roleHolderSession starts from context.Background() at roleHolderReadTimeout, up to roleHolderResolutionAttempts times, plus ReleaseExpiredRoleClaim's own wait - so a slow but live bus can spend the budget before the publish. The result is a role-lane message put on the wire while the caller is answered 503 bus_unavailable; the role lane is core NATS with no JetStream dedupe, and packages/envoy-client/src/transport.ts:281 retries every status at or past 500, so the holder can receive it twice. Found by the security pass; verified in the code by the reviewer. Remedy: refuse an expired or cancelled context before emitting, and correct api.go's comment if the role read is to stay outside the budget.

An unplaceableDeferrals entry whose message never reaches this listener again is never released, and unplaceableDeferralCap of them turn the retry off until the process restarts. The type's comment states this. Not reachable today and not counted as a defect by either thermonuclear pass: the stream's MaxAge is contracts.DeliveryDuplicateWindow, 72 hours, with no MaxMsgs or MaxBytes (internal/bus/stream.go:111-119), against a 60 s window, so an orphan needs a message first delivered within five seconds of a 72-hour expiry. Recorded in the body's Not proven / risk because a change shortening MaxAge toward the retry window makes it real and nothing pins the two against each other.
